CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who injured his left ankle yesterday while on a walk with his wife. He stepped off a curb and landed on it incorrectly. He denies hearing a pop but reports feeling the ankle extend and stretch. Pain is located on the outside of the ankle. He was able to walk back to his house after the incident, though it was painful. Pain has been present for a couple of days. Patient rates pain at 8/10 without medication and 7/10 with ibuprofen or Tylenol. He has been treating the injury with ibuprofen, elevation, ice, and weight-bearing avoidance.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No substantial prior injuries to the left ankle.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen and Tylenol as needed for pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. He and his wife take walks regularly.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Stable, slightly elevated due to pain. Left ankle exam: Ecchymosis and swelling over the lateral malleolus with edema. Positive for tenderness to palpation on the lateral side with swollen soft tissue. No joint laxity appreciated. No bony tenderness to palpation of the foot. Neurovascular exam of left foot: Capillary refill brisk, less than 3 seconds. Strong dorsalis pedis pulses. Motor and sensation intact. Neurovascular exam compared bilaterally and symmetric.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle: No fracture or bony abnormalities appreciated.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex. Continue RICE protocol (rest, ice, compression, elevation). Provided air cast for ankle stabilization. Prescribed crutches with instructions to stay off the leg initially but start walking as tolerated in a few days. Continue NSAIDs to help reduce pain and swelling. Symptoms expected to improve significantly over 4-7 days. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. Patient instructed to return if experiencing significant pain or have any questions or concerns.
